newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CA sale to wrap up soon - chief exec.
newsitem.headline: CA sale to wrap up soon - chief exec.

text.p: Creditanstalt-Bankverein chief executive Guido Schmidt-Chiari on Tuesday said the privatisation of the government's majority stake in the bank would proceed swiftly.
"If we all sit down together again in one year's time, the question (of who buys Creditanstalt) will definitely have been decided," Schmidt-Chiari told the Club of Economic Journalists.

On Monday, the six-year long effort to sell the government's entire 70 percent voting stake in Austria's flagship bank went back to square one when Finance Minister Viktor Klima turned down the only firm bid from an Austro-German-Italian group headed by EA Generali.
Klima said the bid did not match the conditions laid down by the government in October 1995.
Schmidt-Chiari said Klima's rejection of the bid "was not particularly surprising, but of course not pleasing."

Creditanstalt would now work with the state's adviser J.P. Morgan to update the memorandum the U.S. investment house prepared last year and come up with a new procedure for privatisation within the next six to eight weeks.

"We will now do all we can to speed up the process. We owe it to our shareholders to press on with privatisation," he said, but declined to be drawn upon how the bid would be updated. "That's up to the owner (Klima)."
Schmidt-Chiari told journalists after the press conference that the buyer would likely come from the present group of suitors. "The buyer won't come out of the blue."
